cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm keeping this room usable for both of us. Was the sofa always this close to the cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for my yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good, we'll preserve that. Just so I have the layout right: did you move the sofa toward the cupboard?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. I moved the mugs too, so you wouldn't need to open it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Very considerate. I'll work around the yoga space. Are the mugs in your sock drawer part of that arrangement, or am I noticing a second little improvement?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 claims shared-room management; A3 preserves B yoga gain and A5 accepts working around it while asking polite specific questions that draw out rearrangement admissions.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 yoga benefit causes A3 preservation plus move question; B4 mug relocation causes A5 identifying the sock-drawer destination.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants exercise space and B4 tried to compensate for blocked access; A acknowledges both instead of making B a random obstacle.

heightening.evidence: A5 extends the admitted sofa alteration into confirmation of an odd contents arrangement.

specificity.evidence: A1 cupboard/sofa and B2 yoga establish enough spatial stakes without a full floor plan.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 little improvement has an ironic edge but remains a question grounded in B4 helpful account.
